author: Eli
title: 当艺术成为修补：从“可见的修复”到“共织”的全球实践
subtitle: 本周，从TED与POSCA的全球驻留到亚洲艺术双年展，艺术界正在重新定义创作与社会修复的关系
closing: 本周的艺术征选与新闻事件，共同勾勒出一幅全球艺术生态的复杂图景：从“可见的修补”到“共织”，从社区介入到生态想象，艺术正在被重新定义为一种修复性的社会行动。然而，画廊薪酬争议与付费参展模式也提醒我们，修复的前提是承认裂缝的存在。对于创作者而言，本周的行动建议或许是：在申请任何一个项目之前，先问自己——这个项目修补的是什么？是社区的裂痕、生态的断裂，还是仅仅是自己的简历？只有明确了这个问题的答案，才能在艺术场域中找到真正属于自己的位置。

sections.heading: 修补的隐喻：从公共介入到生态想象

image.caption: TED × POSCA 驻留计划 2026 · TED 与 POSCA(Fine Acts 策划)
image.caption_en: TED and POSCA Residency · TED and POSCA (Curated by Fine Acts)

paragraphs.t: 本周最引人注目的动向之一，是TED与POSCA联合发起的全球分布式驻留计划，其2026年主题定为“Visible Mending”（可见的修补）。
与
均指向同一核心概念：艺术作为一种公开的、可被观察的修复行动。这一主题的提出，恰逢全球范围内对艺术社会功能的重新评估——不再满足于作品在美术馆内的静默展示，而是要求艺术家走出工作室，在社区层面实施具有修复性的介入。值得注意的是，该驻留计划特别强调“分布式”模式，即艺术家在其所在社区就地创作，这呼应了格罗伊斯关于策展作为档案与行动的论述：艺术不再是被收藏的对象，而是发生在具体社会关系中的事件。
几乎同时，苏格兰格拉斯哥的Molend Art发起了题为《后——动物信号》的展览征集，探讨动物性、非人感知与生态想象。

这一征集与“Visible Mending”形成了有趣的对照：如果说TED的驻留侧重社会关系的修补，那么Molend Art的展览则试图修复人与非人之间的认知断裂。两者都指向一种超越人类中心主义的艺术实践，但前者更接近参与式艺术的行动逻辑，后者则更偏向生态批评的思辨路径。克莱尔·毕晓普曾批评参与式艺术往往陷入道德说教而缺乏审美张力，而“Visible Mending”主题下的社区介入能否避免这一陷阱，将取决于艺术家如何处理“修补”这一行为本身的美学维度。
另一个值得关注的生态取向项目是法国Fondation François Schneider的“Talents Contemporains - La Terre”竞赛，主题明确为“大地”。

ref.text: Talents Contemporains - La Terre - Abbaye de Pontigny 第一届

paragraphs.t: 该竞赛要求雕塑和装置作品回应大地主题，获奖作品将在Pontigny修道院花园展出。修道院花园作为历史与自然的交汇点，为作品提供了独特的语境——大地不再仅仅是材料或母题，而是成为展示场所本身的一部分。这种将作品嵌入具体自然景观的做法，与TED驻留的社区介入形成空间上的对照：一个是花园中的沉思，一个是社区中的行动。

sections.heading: 共织与感知：亚洲艺术现场的参与式转向

image.caption: 2026亞洲藝術雙年展公布主題與首批參展名單 · 藝術家雜誌社
image.caption_en: 2026 Asian Art Biennial Announces Theme and First Batch of Participants · Artist Magazine

paragraphs.t: 亚洲地区的艺术机构本周同样呈现出强烈的参与式倾向。国立台湾美术馆公布了2026亚洲艺术双年展的主题“MrahulTminun．共织．Co-Weaving”，由吕佩怡策展，首波参展艺术家包括林介文等。

ref.text: 2026亞洲藝術雙年展公布主題與首批參展名單

paragraphs.t: “共织”一词直接指向集体劳作与跨文化编织，与TED的“Visible Mending”形成了跨地域的呼应。两者都强调一种修复性的、联结性的实践，但亚洲双年展更侧重原住民知识与传统工艺的当代转化，而TED驻留则更关注全球社区中的可见行动。这种差异反映了不同文化语境下对“修复”的不同理解：在台湾，“共织”可能意味着对殖民历史与离散经验的缝合；在西方，“修补”则更多指向资本主义社会关系的修复。
香港的deTour 2026设计节以“Better, Not Perfect: Prototypes for Tomorrow”为主题公开征集创意方案。

ref.text: deTour 2026 创意方案公开征集

paragraphs.t: 这一主题明确拒绝完美主义，拥抱原型思维，与“Visible Mending”的修补逻辑一脉相承——两者都认可不完美与过程的价值。deTour提供最高15万港币的制作赞助，这种对原型制作的直接资助，降低了创作者的风险，鼓励试错与迭代。这种机制与传统的艺术奖项不同，更接近设计思维中的敏捷开发模式。
台南市美术馆在TAM⁺艺术之森推出的展览“魔法蓝图生成中”同样强调参与和共作。

ref.text: 臺南市美術館TAM⁺藝術之森「魔法藍圖生成中」，以共創展覽與工作坊串連跨世代參與，延展城市空間的感知經驗

paragraphs.t: 该展览结合法国艺术家Laure Catugier的驻村与版印创作，通过工作坊引导市民参与，探索城市空间与地方记忆。这种将国际艺术家与本地社区联结的模式，与TED驻留的分布式逻辑相似，但更侧重于城市空间感知的延展。值得注意的是，该展览的展期仅为7月3日至8月30日，这种短期、高强度的参与式项目，考验的是机构组织社区动员的能力，而非作品的永恒性。

sections.heading: 机构与市场的裂缝：薪酬争议与展览伦理

image.caption: 开普敦画廊被指控拖欠薪酬和扣留艺术品 · Hyperallergic
image.caption_en: Cape Town Gallery Accused of Withholding Pay and Artworks · Hyperallergic

paragraphs.t: 本周国际艺术界最令人不安的新闻来自南非：艺术家Kate Gottgens指控开普敦SMAC画廊扣留其画作并延迟付款，一幅作品甚至在米兰艺博会后四年未归还。

ref.text: 开普敦画廊被指控拖欠薪酬和扣留艺术品

paragraphs.t: 画廊否认指控，将延迟归因于进出口问题。这一事件暴露了艺术市场中权力不对等的普遍问题——尤其是当画廊与艺术家之间缺乏透明的合同保障时。布尔迪厄的场域理论在此刻显得尤为锋利：艺术场域看似自主，实则充斥着经济资本与文化资本的博弈。画廊作为场域中的中间人，掌握着展览、销售、物流等环节的话语权，而艺术家往往处于弱势。Gottgens的案例并非孤例，它提醒所有创作者：在追求展览机会的同时，必须警惕商业画廊可能带来的风险。
与这一负面新闻形成对比的是，本周多个机构提供了相对公平的征集机制。例如，利物浦的《遁入绿林》展览明确标注“销售0抽成但不保证成交”，并因商业场地要求不接受全裸正面作品。
这种坦率的条件设定，虽然限制了创作自由，但至少避免了事后纠纷。巴黎臻艺画廊的《悬置》展览同样实行0抽成，但要求入选者支付200英镑参展费。
这种“付费参展”模式在小型画廊中常见，其伦理争议在于：它可能筛选出经济资本充裕但艺术质量未必最高的申请者。然而，对于缺乏机构支持的独立艺术家而言，这或许是获得展出机会的唯一途径。
中国美术馆的暑期夜场开放则从另一个侧面反映了机构与公众的关系：每日新增2000个预约名额，实行分时段错峰入场。

ref.oid: news-h5kpmn-中国美术馆2026暑期夜场开放-每日新增预约名额2000个
ref.text: 中国美术馆2026暑期夜场开放 每日新增预约名额2000个

paragraphs.t: 这种延时开放政策，表面上是服务公众，实则暗含机构对“文化民主化”的承诺。然而，当美术馆成为网红打卡地，夜场开放是否真的促进了深度艺术体验，还是仅仅制造了流量？这一问题值得持续观察。

sections.heading: 征选机制：全球化与地方性的张力

image.caption: 未来世代艺术奖 · 维克多·平丘克基金会 / PinchukArtCentre
image.caption_en: Future Generation Art Prize · Victor Pinchuk Foundation / PinchukArtCentre

paragraphs.t: 本周截止的多个奖项与驻留项目，揭示了全球艺术征选机制中的结构性张力。未来世代艺术奖面向全球35岁以下艺术家，提供10万美元主奖，由维克多·平丘克基金会支持。
这一奖项的全球化野心显而易见——它试图通过高额奖金和知名基金会背书，建立一套超越地域的艺术价值评判标准。然而，这种全球性往往意味着西方标准的隐性主导。相比之下，东京的TOKAS-Emerging 2027明确限定“日本国内35岁以下艺术家”。
这种地方性的限定，既是对本土艺术生态的保护，也可能导致与国际对话的缺失。
中国的征选活动同样呈现出这种张力。约翰·莫尔绘画奖（中国）面向生活创作在中国境内的绘画创作者，报名费200元人民币。
这一奖项源自英国，在中国落地后形成了独特的双轨制：既保留英国奖项的品牌价值，又适应中国本土的创作环境。而中国美协主办的第五届青年漆画展览则严格限定年龄（45周岁以下）和媒介（漆画），体现了体制内展览对传统工艺的扶持。

ref.oid: search-caanet-中国美协艺委会青年展系列-第五届青年漆画展览征稿通知
ref.text: 中国美协艺委会青年展系列：第五届青年漆画展览征稿通知

paragraphs.t: 这两种征选逻辑——国际品牌本土化与体制内行业细分——并行不悖，反映了中国艺术生态的多元性。
值得注意的还有香港浸会大学的国际作家工作坊，面向居住在香港以外的国际作家，提供一个月驻留。

ref.text: 香港浸会大学 国际作家工作坊 2027

paragraphs.t: 这一项目与TED驻留形成了有趣的对照：前者是传统意义上的“作家驻留”，强调文学创作与文化交流；后者则是“社区介入驻留”，强调公共行动与视觉艺术。两者对“驻留”的不同定义，折射出文学与视觉艺术在当代语境下的分岔：文学驻留仍以文本生产为核心，视觉艺术驻留则越来越注重关系美学与社区参与。

en.title: When Art Becomes Repair: From 'Visible Mending' to 'Co-Weaving' in Global Practice
en.subtitle: This week, from TED and POSCA's global residency to the Asian Art Biennial, the art world is redefining the relationship between creation and social repair.
en.closing: This week's art calls and news events together sketch a complex picture of the global art ecosystem: from 'Visible Mending' to 'Co-Weaving,' from community intervention to ecological imagination, art is being redefined as a restorative social action. However, gallery pay disputes and pay-to-exhibit models also remind us that repair presupposes acknowledging cracks. For creators, this week's action suggestion might be: before applying for any project, ask yourself—what does this project mend? A community rift, an ecological rupture, or merely your own résumé? Only by clarifying this question can one find their true place in the art field.

sections.heading: The Metaphor of Mending: From Public Intervention to Ecological Imagination

paragraphs.t: One of the most notable developments this week is the globally distributed residency program jointly launched by TED and POSCA, with its 2026 theme set as 'Visible Mending.'
and

both point to the same core concept: art as a public, observable act of repair. This theme emerges at a time when the social function of art is being reassessed worldwide—no longer satisfied with silent display within museum walls, it demands that artists step out of the studio and implement restorative interventions at the community level. Notably, the residency program emphasizes a 'distributed' model, where artists create work in their own communities, echoing Groys's discussion of curation as archive and action: art is no longer an object to be collected but an event occurring within specific social relations.
Almost simultaneously, Molend Art in Glasgow, Scotland, launched an open call for the exhibition 'Post—Animal Signals,' exploring animality, non-human perception, and ecological imagination.

This call forms an interesting contrast with 'Visible Mending': while the TED residency focuses on repairing social relations, the Molend Art exhibition seeks to mend the cognitive rift between humans and non-humans. Both point to an artistic practice that transcends anthropocentrism, but the former aligns more with the action logic of participatory art, while the latter leans toward the speculative path of ecological criticism. Claire Bishop has criticized participatory art for often falling into moralizing without aesthetic tension; whether community interventions under the 'Visible Mending' theme can avoid this trap will depend on how artists handle the aesthetic dimension of the act of 'mending' itself.

Another ecologically oriented project worth noting is the 'Talents Contemporains - La Terre' competition by the Fondation François Schneider in France, with the explicit theme of 'Earth.' [[19: Talents Contemporains - La Terre - Abbaye de Pontigny, First Edition]] The competition calls for sculptures and installations responding to the earth theme, with winning works to be exhibited in the garden of the Pontigny Abbey. The abbey garden, as a meeting point of history and nature, provides a unique context for the works—the earth is no longer merely a material or motif but becomes part of the exhibition site itself. This embedding of works in a specific natural landscape forms a spatial contrast with the community interventions of the TED residency: one is contemplation in a garden, the other action in a community.

sections.heading: Co-Weaving and Perception: The Participatory Turn in the Asian Art Scene

paragraphs.t: Art institutions in Asia also show a strong participatory tendency this week. The National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts announced the theme of the 2026 Asian Art Biennial, 'MrahulTminun．Co-Weaving,' curated by Lu Pei-Yi, with the first batch of participating artists including Lin Jie-Wen. [[40: 2026 Asian Art Biennial Announces Theme and First Participating Artists]] The term 'co-weaving' directly points to collective labor and cross-cultural weaving, echoing 'Visible Mending' across regions. Both emphasize a restorative, connective practice, but the Asian Biennial focuses more on the contemporary transformation of indigenous knowledge and traditional crafts, while the TED residency is more concerned with visible action in global communities. This difference reflects varying understandings of 'repair' in different cultural contexts: in Taiwan, 'co-weaving' may signify the stitching together of colonial history and diasporic experience; in the West, 'mending' often refers to repairing capitalist social relations.
Hong Kong's deTour 2026 Design Festival issued an open call for creative proposals under the theme 'Better, Not Perfect: Prototypes for Tomorrow.'

ref.text: deTour 2026 Open Call for Creative Proposals

paragraphs.t: This theme explicitly rejects perfectionism and embraces prototype thinking, aligning with the mending logic of 'Visible Mending'—both recognize the value of imperfection and process. deTour offers a production sponsorship of up to HKD 150,000, directly supporting prototyping, reducing creators' risk, and encouraging trial and error. This mechanism differs from traditional art awards, resembling the agile development model in design thinking.

The exhibition 'Magic Blueprints in Progress' at the TAM⁺ Art Forest of the Tainan Art Museum also emphasizes participation and co-creation. [[34: Tainan Art Museum TAM⁺ Art Forest 'Magic Blueprints in Progress': Co-creative Exhibitions and Workshops Connecting Generations, Extending Urban Spatial Perception]] The exhibition combines the residency of French artist Laure Catugier with printmaking, engaging citizens through workshops to explore urban space and local memory. This model of linking international artists with local communities resembles the distributed logic of the TED residency but focuses more on extending urban spatial perception. Notably, the exhibition runs only from July 3 to August 30; such short-term, high-intensity participatory projects test the institution's ability to mobilize the community rather than the permanence of the works.

sections.heading: Cracks in Institutions and Markets: Pay Disputes and Exhibition Ethics

paragraphs.t: The most unsettling news in the international art world this week comes from South Africa: artist Kate Gottgens accused SMAC Gallery in Cape Town of withholding her paintings and delaying payment, with one work not returned four years after the Milan art fair.

ref.text: Cape Town Gallery Accused of Withholding Pay and Artworks

paragraphs.t: The gallery denies the allegations, attributing the delay to import-export issues. This incident exposes the widespread power imbalance in the art market—especially when transparent contractual safeguards are lacking between galleries and artists. Bourdieu's field theory becomes particularly sharp here: the art field appears autonomous but is rife with struggles between economic and cultural capital. Galleries, as intermediaries in the field, hold sway over exhibition, sales, logistics, and other aspects, while artists are often vulnerable. Gottgens's case is not isolated; it reminds all creators to be wary of the risks posed by commercial galleries while pursuing exhibition opportunities.

In contrast to this negative news, several institutions this week offered relatively fair call mechanisms. For example, the exhibition 'Into the Greenwood' in Liverpool explicitly states '0% commission on sales but no guarantee of sale' and, due to commercial venue requirements, does not accept full-frontal nude works.

Such candid conditions, though limiting creative freedom, at least avoid post-hoc disputes. The exhibition 'Suspension' at Galerie Zhen in Paris also operates with 0% commission but requires selected artists to pay a participation fee of £200.

This 'pay-to-exhibit' model is common in small galleries, and its ethical controversy lies in potentially selecting applicants with sufficient economic capital rather than the highest artistic quality. However, for independent artists lacking institutional support, it may be the only way to gain exhibition opportunities.

The National Art Museum of China's summer evening openings reflect another aspect of the institution-public relationship: adding 2,000 daily reservation slots with staggered entry times. [[36: National Art Museum of China 2026 Summer Evening Opening Adds 2,000 Daily Reservation Slots]] This extended-hours policy, ostensibly serving the public, implicitly carries the institution's commitment to 'cultural democratization.' Yet, when museums become social media hotspots, do evening openings truly foster deep art experiences, or merely generate traffic? This question warrants ongoing observation.

sections.heading: Selection Mechanisms: The Tension Between Globalization and Locality

paragraphs.t: Several awards and residencies closing this week reveal structural tensions in global art selection mechanisms. The Future Generation Art Prize, open to artists under 35 worldwide, offers a $100,000 main prize, supported by the Victor Pinchuk Foundation.

The global ambition of this prize is evident—it seeks to establish a set of art value criteria transcending geography through high prize money and a renowned foundation's endorsement. However, such globality often implies the implicit dominance of Western standards. In contrast, TOKAS-Emerging 2027 in Tokyo explicitly limits eligibility to 'artists under 35 residing in Japan.'
This local restriction both protects the domestic art ecosystem and may lead to a lack of international dialogue.
Chinese selection activities also exhibit this tension. The John Moores Painting Prize (China) is open to painting creators living and working in China, with an entry fee of RMB 200.

Originating in the UK, this prize has developed a unique dual-track system in China: retaining the brand value of the British award while adapting to the local creative environment. Meanwhile, the Fifth Youth Lacquer Painting Exhibition, organized by the Chinese Artists Association's Art Committee, strictly limits age (under 45) and medium (lacquer painting), reflecting the institutional support for traditional crafts. [[21: Chinese Artists Association Art Committee Youth Exhibition Series: Call for Submissions for the Fifth Youth Lacquer Painting Exhibition]] These two selection logics—localization of international brands and sector-specific institutional exhibitions—coexist, reflecting the diversity of China's art ecosystem.

Also noteworthy is the International Writers Workshop at Hong Kong Baptist University, open to international writers residing outside Hong Kong for a one-month residency. [[15: Hong Kong Baptist University International Writers Workshop 2027]] This project forms an interesting contrast with the TED residency: the former is a traditional 'writers' residency' emphasizing literary creation and cultural exchange; the latter is a 'community intervention residency' emphasizing public action and visual art. Their different definitions of 'residency' reflect the divergence between literature and visual art in the contemporary context: literary residencies still center on text production, while visual art residencies increasingly focus on relational aesthetics and community engagement.
